newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale still studying Airjet 70 launch.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale still studying Airjet 70 launch.

text.p: State-owned Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot said no decision has been taken on a launch of the 70-seater Airjet programme but the company was reviewing its regional planes activities.

Aerospatiale is a partner in Aero International (Regional), AI(R), the venture which markets the Avro RJ jet made by British Aerospace Plc (BAe) and the ATR turboprop built by Aerospatiale and Alenia, part of Italy's Finmeccanica.
"What is certain is that at the moment we have not decided to invest the resources of our house in a new regional plane project," he said.

AI(R) has been considering a launch of its first new product, the Airjet 70, with a stake of up to 50 percent to be held by the Korean Commercial Development Consortium of South Korea and Taiwanese firms.
Airjet's development costs are estimated at $1 billion.
Industry analysts consider the long-term future of AI(R) doubtful without the Airjet, which would have brought its product range up to date.
Michot said that following BAe's recent decision to halt production of its J41 Jetstream turboprop plane and Alenia's cash shortage, Aerospatiale was reviewing its own interests.
The regional plane market suffers from a lack of orders and stiff competition. BAe has said it was losing one million pounds on each J41 30-seater that it sold.
Aerospatiale's head of the aeronautics division, Claude Terrazzoni said, "It is possible that the chairman of AI(R) will not be very positive."
Michot said AI(R) could get by with sales of around 40 ATR planes a year but the big decision was how Aerospatiale should allocate capital around the group to develop its business.
Aerospatiale also has to consider its commitments on the worldwide fleet of between 600-700 ATRs which need to be maintained and supplied, Michot said.
A decision by the AI(R) partners to pull out of Airjet would leave a near monopoly to Bombardier'S Canadair unit, which makes the CRJ 7000 70-seater jet.
Michot said an announcement on the Airjet could be made at the Paris Air Show, which opens on June 14.
